sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Hannover has the most ambitious plan for its inner city of the cities we cover, and has so far changed fees only at the margins. On 29 September 2022 the council adopted an inner-city concept as a framework to 2035, which the mayor called a broad consensus for a change towards a car-free inner city [1]. In September 2023 the city presented a plan, not yet adopted by the council at that time, to make the core almost car-free by 2030, with on-street parking largely disappearing and cars led to the existing garages, which the city described as not nearly fully used; we did not find whether the council later adopted it [4]. The city's FAQ of October 2023 counts about 9,630 spaces in public garages in the inner city, about 3,843 in public street space and roughly 5,800 on private land [13]. On 18 December 2025 the council adopted the Masterplan Mobilität 2035, one of whose action areas is to establish city parking management [11].

On fees, the free 10-minute ticket was abolished in May 2023 and three resident zones started in the Südstadt, when the highest on-street rate was 2.60 euros an hour [2]. In August 2025 a press report on an internal draft said on-street parking might rise from 2.60 to 4.80 euros an hour inside the Cityring; this was only a draft, and the IHK Hannover rejected it [7][8]. The city's tariff page read in October 2026 shows 1.30 euros per half hour in the inner-city zone, which is 2.60 euros an hour, with E-plate cars free until the end of 2026 [14]; we found no source that the 4.80 euro draft was adopted. What the council did adopt on 18 December 2025 is a new fee ordinance that raises the annual resident permit from 30.70 to 96 euros, which the city says took effect on 1 February 2026 [10][15]. Hannover's Umweltzone ended on 22 February 2024 [5].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text:
The development is mainly in resident zones and park-and-ride. Resident zones now cover Mitte, F, G and H (since March 2025), J (since November 2025) and the Südstadt zones, and the city says studies are under way for Nordstadt, Vahrenwald, List, Zoo, Bult and Südstadt [15]. The hanova company opened Parkhaus Nordstadt at the Klinikum Nordstadt in May 2023 with 141 spaces and four charging points [3].

On park and ride, the Region Hannover's traffic management centre equipped pilot sites with occupancy sensors in 2021, including Wissenschaftspark Marienwerder and Nordhafen, and said it wanted to use free P+R spaces to steer event traffic [0]. The Hermann-Ehlers-Allee site opened on 20 March 2024 with 70 spaces and live occupancy; by April 2024 the regional Infra company said commuters were using it only hesitantly, while the 170-space site at Hemmingen was often full [6]. The city's Arena page lists Marienwerder and Nordhafen as free, around-the-clock P+R sites [12].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
hanova describes itself as Hannover's largest garage operator and lists 8 inner-city garages, 4 district garages and 3 car parks with about 5,500 spaces; the first hour costs 2.50 euros at five inner-city garages, 3 euros at Oper/Kröpcke and Windmühlenstraße and 2 euros at Hbf/Raschplatz [3][16]. The regional traffic management centre says there are 28,000 spaces near the Messe, with a guidance system on the Messering leading traffic to the lots for each fair [17]. We did not find sources on other garage operators.

Our Hannover data are limited to three regional park-and-ride sites, not the city's garages: Marienwerder (310 spaces), Nordhafen (180) and Hermann-Ehlers-Allee (69 in the feed against the 70 the region states [6]), measured since 26 September 2026. Occupancy averaged about 21% on weekdays and 12% at weekends, weighted by spaces. Nordhafen averaged 25% and Marienwerder 23% on weekdays, falling to 19% and 10% at weekends, and neither came close to full; Hermann-Ehlers-Allee averaged 3% and peaked at 19%, consistent with the regional company's remark about commuters using it only hesitantly [6]. This says nothing about the inner-city garages that the concept relies on, and the window is four weeks.
